# Ezekiel 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** He said to me, "Son of man, eat what is in front of you — eat this scroll. Then go and speak to the people of Israel."

**2** So I opened my mouth, and He fed me the scroll.

**3** "Eat it all," He told me. "Fill your stomach with it." So I ate it, and it tasted as sweet as honey in my mouth.

**4** Then He said, "Now go to the people of Israel and give them My message.

**5** I'm not sending you to foreigners who speak a strange language —

**6** not to distant nations whose words you can't understand. If I had sent you to them, they actually would have listened!

**7** But the people of Israel won't listen to you — because they refuse to listen to Me. The whole nation is stubborn and hardheaded.

**8** So I'm making you just as tough as they are — your face as hard as their faces, your determination as fierce as their stubbornness.

**9** I'm making your forehead like diamond — harder than flint. Don't be afraid of them. Don't let their hostile looks break you down, because they are a rebellious people."

**10** He also said, "Son of man, take to heart every word I say to you. Listen carefully.

**11** Then go to your people in exile and deliver this message: 'This is what the Lord GOD says' — whether they listen or not."

**12** Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a tremendous rumbling sound — "Praise the glory of the LORD from His dwelling place!"

**13** It was the sound of the living creatures' wings brushing against each other, and the rumbling of the wheels, and a great thunderous roar.

**14** The Spirit picked me up and carried me away. I went feeling bitter and angry, with the LORD's hand gripping me powerfully.

**15** I arrived at Tel-abib, where the Jewish exiles lived beside the Chebar River. I sat among them for seven days, completely stunned.

**16** After seven days, the LORD spoke to me again:

**17** "Son of man, I have appointed you as a watchman for Israel. Whenever I give you a message, you must warn the people immediately.

**18** If I warn the wicked that they will die, and you fail to pass on the warning — if you don't tell them to change their ways to save their lives — they will die in their sins, but I will hold you responsible for their deaths.

**19** However, if you do warn them and they still refuse to repent, they will die in their sins, but you will have saved yourself.

**20** And if a righteous person turns away from doing right and starts doing evil, and I put an obstacle in their path, they will die. Because you didn't warn them, they will die in their sin. Their previous good deeds won't count for anything — and I will hold you responsible.

**21** But if you warn righteous people not to sin, and they listen and don't sin, they will live. And you will have saved yourself."

**22** The LORD's hand was on me there, and He said, "Get up and go out to the valley. I will speak to you there."

**23** So I got up and went to the valley — and the glory of the LORD was standing there, just as I had seen it by the Chebar River. I fell facedown.

**24** But the Spirit entered me, stood me on my feet, and spoke to me: "Go home and shut yourself inside your house.

**25** Son of man, they are going to tie you up with ropes so you can't go out among the people.

**26** I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so you'll be silent — unable to rebuke them, even though they are rebels.

**27** But when I have something for you to say, I will open your mouth, and you will tell them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.' Whoever listens will listen; whoever refuses will refuse — they are a rebellious people.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **3:1-3**: Eating a scroll of doom and having it taste like honey — that's the paradox of hearing from God. The message is devastating, but the encounter itself is sweet.

- **3:14-15**: Ezekiel doesn't skip to his assignment full of enthusiasm. He's bitter, angry, and overwhelmed. God's hand is 'strong' on him — almost forceful. Real calling isn't always inspiring; sometimes it's crushing.

- **3:17-21**: The watchman image is sobering. God isn't asking Ezekiel to save anyone — just to sound the alarm. But if the watchman stays silent? The blood is on his hands. Silence is not neutral.

— PNEUMA
